title: Post‑Outage Client Communication and Recovery Options Menu
content:
Purpose:
This is a customer-facing communications draft intended to be used across three channels: status.redwood.com update, targeted email to impacted tenants, and a short enterprise Slack/Teams note for assigned account contacts. It focuses on (1) clear plain-language explanation, (2) timeline and root-cause summary, (3) concrete recovery choices the tenant can opt into, and (4) evidence/reconciliation to allow customers to validate results.

Executive summary (one paragraph for status page):
Between 2026-07-07 08:13 UTC and 2026-07-07 10:22 UTC Redwood experienced degraded inference responses for a subset of hosted API requests in the us-east-1 region. Root cause: a cascading cache eviction combined with a routing roll that temporarily routed long-lived KV caches to warm hosts without synchronized warmup, causing elevated tail latency and truncated streaming responses for affected sessions. We mitigated the issue by reverting the routing change, performing a controlled cache warmup, and applying a safety throttle for single-tenant burst traffic. Most customers saw service recovery by 10:22 UTC; some long-running streaming sessions were impacted and may need replay.

Suggested statuspage update (short):
Title: Degraded responses in us-east-1 — resolved
Summary: Resolved — degraded inference responses affecting a subset of requests. Root cause: cache/routing mismatch during a rollout. Impact: elevated latency and occasional truncated streaming responses. Mitigation: rollback and coordinated cache warmup. Customer action: if you observed truncated or missing output, follow the Replay & Verification steps below.

Targeted email subject lines (choose one):
- Important: Action available for requests impacted by short-lived inference truncation (us-east-1)
- We fixed a routing/cache issue — next steps for reconciling impacted responses

Email body (concise customer-ready):
Hi <CustomerContact>,

We want to make you aware of a service event that may have affected some of your requests in us-east-1 on 2026-07-07 between 08:13–10:22 UTC. During the event some streaming responses were truncated or returned with elevated latency. We have implemented a rollback and cache warmup — the platform is stable.

What you can do now (Recovery Options Menu):
1) Opt into a server-side replay (recommended for important transactions) — Redwood will re-run affected requests using the pinned model version and attach a verification digest showing token-by-token parity where available. Choose this if your application requires exact completeness.
2) Request a best-effort merge (fast) — Redwood will attempt to reconstruct missing segments using cached context; best when completeness is desirable but latency matters.
3) No action — if your application ignores occasional truncation or you have client-side retry logic, no action required.

How to request a replay or merge: reply to this email with the Incident ID INC-2026-0710 and the tenantId(s) you want reconciled, or open a ticket JIRA-OPS-4521 and select the "Replay / Merge" option. For enterprise partners we can coordinate a bulk reconciliation window.

Verification & Evidence:
- Each replay attempt will provide a signed evidence bundle that includes: original request id, original timestamp, model version and seed, token-level output diff (where available), and an operator approval log.
- We include a short checklist to help you validate reconstructed responses locally.

Compensation & SLAs:
If you rely on strict SLAs and need formal credit, please reference your support contract and the incident ID; customer-success will coordinate the SLA review.

Root cause (technical summary for customer appendix):
During a scheduled routing rollout we introduced a change that shifted a subset of long-lived KV/cache pointers to a new pool. Those hosts had not received concurrent KV warmup and our routing policy sent active sessions to them. When the runtime attempted to resolve prefixes the caches were incomplete, leading to fall-back behavior that increased per-request latency and, for some streaming sessions, caused the generator to hit an internal truncation safeguard. The combination of warmup gaps and aggressive concurrency resulted in the observed symptoms.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-07-07 07:55 — Pre-rollout checks showed some evictions scheduled for later windows.
- 2026-07-07 08:05 — Rollout initiated (incremental routing change).
- 2026-07-07 08:13 — First elevated tail latency alerts; streaming session errors detected for tenant shards A1..A3.
- 2026-07-07 08:25 — Automated mitigation attempted (traffic throttle) but insufficient to prevent truncation.
- 2026-07-07 08:46 — Rollback decision made; rollback executed across us-east-1.
- 2026-07-07 09:10 — Cache warmup scripts started and traffic gradually shifted back to warmed hosts.
- 2026-07-07 10:22 — Platform returned to baseline for majority of traffic; monitoring in steady state.
- 2026-07-07 12:00 — Postmortem investigation started; customer outreach prep.

Impact matrix (customer-facing):
- Scope: ~2.1% of active tenant requests in us-east-1 during window (weighted toward multi-turn streaming sessions).
- Severity: intermittent truncation (low to medium impact depending on application tolerance).
- Data integrity: there is no evidence of data loss from customer payloads; only response outputs were incomplete.

Replay & validation details (what the replay shows):
- Replays will be executed against the same model hash/version that served the original request and with the original prompt where available.
- Because of nondeterminism in some model variants, we provide a token-diff and a "semantic parity" score that indicates whether the replayed output is functionally equivalent (per our eval heuristics) even if tokenization differs.

Checklist for customers before requesting replay:
- Identify the time window and request IDs (if you log them) — we can also query by tenant and approximate timestamp.
- Decide whether you prefer exact token parity (slower server-side deterministic replay) or fast best-effort reconstruction.
- Provide a contact person and a preferred reconciliation SLAT (24h/72h).

Operator notes (internal quick reference):
- Priority: enterprise tenants with active SLAs and customers reporting data losses get priority for deterministic replays.
- Runbook steps: validate rollback state, confirm cache warmup completion, run targeted replay job per tenant, attach evidence bundle, notify customer.
- Escalation: if semantic parity < 0.9 for deterministic replay, escalate to Applied ML for model-seed investigation.

Pre-approved comms snippets for quick publishing:
Public statuspage: "Resolved — degraded responses in us-east-1 due to cache/routing mismatch during rollout. Mitigations: rollback and cache warmup. If you observed truncated outputs, see your tenant inbox for reconciliation options."
Email header for impacted tenants: "Action available: Replay or reconstruct responses impacted during short-lived us-east-1 disruption"
Enterprise Slack/Teams: "Investigated: routing-induced cache warmup gap. Platform stable. Reach out to CS with INC-2026-0710 for replay options."

Open questions & followups for engineering/product:
- Preventative: add pre-warm hooks in routing rollout pipeline and require successful warmup threshold before traffic migration.
- Observability: add a streaming-session completeness metric and a TTL-aware cache-warmup timer to alert earlier.
- Cost/ops: run a small kaizen to quantify additional warmup duration vs. risk reduction.

Next steps for CS & account teams (actionable):
1) Send targeted email (use this doc) to customers who logged streaming errors.
2) Collect replay requests in the dedicated JIRA queue and tag with priority.
3) Coordinate with Applied ML to schedule deterministic replays for top-priority enterprise tenants.
4) Publish short statuspage update and link to this customer-facing appendix.

Appendix: Minimal verification checklist we will include with evidence bundle:
- Request ID and timestamp matches customer logs.
- Model version/hash and seed recorded.
- Token-level diff (if deterministic replay).
- Operator approval timestamp.

Contact: Aisha Patel (Customer Success) — aisha.patel@redwoodinfra.com — include Incident ID INC-2026-0710 in subject.

Draft notes: keep this doc for internal review; once approved turn "status" to final and publish the statuspage snippet plus email template from the approved copy.
